cases.sentence: А как выйду замуж, будет уже не до любви, ___ заглушат все старое.
cases.explain: «новые заботы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Masha. To love without hope, to spend whole years waiting for something. … But when I marry, there will be no time left for love, new cares will smother all the old feelings. And, anyway, it will be a change, you know. Shall we have another?

cases.sentence: Мой учитель не очень-то умен, но ___ и бедняк и меня сильно любит.
cases.explain: «добрый человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Masha. My schoolmaster is not very brilliant, but he is a good-natured man, and poor, and he is very much in love with me. I am sorry for him. And I am sorry for his old mother. Well, let me wish you all happiness. Don’t remember evil against me shakes hands with him warmly. I am very grateful for your friendly interest. Send me your books and be sure to put in an inscription. Only don’t write, “To my honoured friend,” but write simply, “To Marya who belongs nowhere and has no object in life.” Goodbye! Goes out.

cases.sentence: Я прошу вас принять от меня на память вот этот ___.
cases.explain: «маленький медальон» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Nina. We are parting and … perhaps we shall never meet again. Won’t you please take this little medallion as a parting gift? I had your initials engraved on one side of it … and on the other the title of your book, Days and Nights.

cases.sentence: — неделю назад, когда вы были в ___…
cases.explain: «светлом платье» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Trigorin. I shall think of you. I shall think of you as you were on that sunny day—do you remember?—a week ago, when you were wearing a light dress … we were talking … there was a white seagull lying on the seat.

cases.sentence: Мы разговаривали… еще тогда на скамье лежала ___.
cases.explain: «белая чайка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Trigorin. I shall think of you. I shall think of you as you were on that sunny day—do you remember?—a week ago, when you were wearing a light dress … we were talking … there was a white seagull lying on the seat.

cases.sentence: (Смеется.) Будет закладка ___ и все такое…
cases.explain: «земского дома» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Sorin. Nothing particular, but still … laughs. There will be the laying of the foundation-stone of the Zemstvo hall, and all that sort of thing. One longs to shake oneself free from this stagnant existence, if only for an hour or two. I’ve been too long on the shelf like some old cigarette-holder. I have ordered the horses for one o’clock; we’ll set off at the same time.

cases.sentence: Хочется хоть на час-другой воспрянуть от этой пескариной жизни, а то очень уж я залежался, точно ___.
cases.explain: «старый мундштук» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Ты великодушная, ___.
cases.explain: «благородная женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Sorin. Begins to whistle. Quite so. Forgive me, my dear, don’t be cross. I believe you. … You are a generous, noble-hearted woman.

cases.sentence: Аркадина (достает из аптечного шкапа йодоформ и ящик с ___).
cases.explain: «перевязочным материалом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Madame Arkadin. Takes out of the medicine cupboard some iodoform and a box with bandaging material. The doctor is late.

cases.sentence: То была минута ___, когда я не мог владеть собою.
cases.explain: «безумного отчаяния» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Treplev. No, mother. It was a moment of mad despair when I could not control myself. It won’t happen again. Kisses her hand. You have such clever hands. I remember, long ago, when you were still acting at the Imperial Theatre—I was little then—there was a fight in our yard and a washerwoman, one of the tenants, was badly beaten. Do you remember? She was picked up senseless … you looked after her, took her remedies and washed her children in a tub. Don’t you remember?

cases.sentence: (Целует ей руку.) У тебя ___.
cases.explain: «золотые руки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Treplev. No, mother. It was a moment of mad despair when I could not control myself. It won’t happen again. Kisses her hand. You have such clever hands. I remember, long ago, when you were still acting at the Imperial Theatre—I was little then—there was a fight in our yard and a washerwoman, one of the tenants, was badly beaten. Do you remember? She was picked up senseless … you looked after her, took her remedies and washed her children in a tub. Don’t you remember?

cases.sentence: Людям не талантливым, но с претензиями, ничего больше не остается, как порицать ___.
cases.explain: «настоящие таланты» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Madame Arkadin. That’s envy. There’s nothing left for people who have pretension without talent but to attack real talent. Much comfort in that, I must say!

cases.sentence: (В раздумье.) Отчего в этом призыве ___ послышалась мне печаль и мое сердце так болезненно сжалось?..
cases.explain: «чистой души» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Trigorin. Impatiently. Yes, yes. Musing. Why is it that I feel so much sorrow in that appeal from a pure soul and that it wrings my heart so painfully? “If ever my life can be of use to you, come and take it.” To Madame Arkadin. Let us stay one day longer.

cases.sentence: Будь ты тоже трезва, будь умна, рассудительна, умоляю тебя, взгляни на все это как ___…
cases.explain: «истинный друг» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Trigorin. You be sober too, be sensible and reasonable, I implore you; look at it all as a true friend should. Presses her hand. You are capable of sacrifice. Be a friend to me, let me be free!

cases.sentence: Аркадина (в ___).
cases.explain: «сильном волнении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Madame Arkadin. In violent agitation. Are you so enthralled?

cases.sentence: Любовь ___?
cases.explain: «провинциальной девочки» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Madame Arkadin. The love of a provincial girl? Oh, how little you know yourself!

cases.sentence: Я ___, со мною нельзя говорить так…
cases.explain: «обыкновенная женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Madame Arkadin. Trembling. No, no! I am an ordinary woman, you can’t talk like that to me. Don’t torture me, Boris. It terrifies me.

cases.sentence: Неужели я уже так стара и безобразна, что со мною можно, не стесняясь, говорить о ___?
cases.explain: «других женщинах» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Madame Arkadin. Am I so old and ugly that you don’t mind talking of other women to me? Puts her arms round him and kisses him. Oh, you are mad! My wonderful, splendid darling. … You are the last page of my life! Falls on her knees. My joy, my pride, my bliss! … embraces his knees. If you forsake me even for one hour I shall not survive it, I shall go mad, my marvellous, magnificent one, my master. …

cases.sentence: Ты ___ моей жизни!
cases.explain: «последняя страница» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: И этот лоб мой, и глаза мои, и эти прекрасные ___ тоже мои…
cases.explain: «шелковистые волосы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Madame Arkadin. Let them, I am not ashamed of my love for you kisses his hands. My treasure, you desperate boy, you want to be mad, but I won’t have it, I won’t let you … laughs. You are mine … mine. … This forehead is mine, and these eyes, and this lovely silky hair is mine too … you are mine all over. You are so gifted, so clever, the best of all modern writers, you are the one hope of Russia. … You have so much truthfulness, simplicity, freshness, healthy humour. … In one touch you can give all the essential characteristics of a person or a landscape, your characters are living. One can’t read you without delight! You think this is exaggerated? That I am flattering you? But look into my eyes … look. … Do I look like a liar? You see, I am the only one who can appreciate you; I am the only one who tells you the truth, my precious, wonderful darling. … Are you coming? Yes? You won’t abandon me? …

cases.sentence: В ___, куда тебе спешить?
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Madame Arkadin. To herself. Now he is mine! In an easy tone as though nothing had happened. But, of course, if you like, you can stay. I’ll go by myself and you can come afterwards, a week later. After all, why should you be in a hurry?

cases.sentence: Остановитесь в «___»…
cases.explain: «Славянском базаре» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Trigorin. Looking round. Stay at the Slavyansky Bazaar … Let me know at once … Molchanovka, Groholsky House. … I am in a hurry … a pause.
